Although linguistic masking schemes (named entities and noun phrases) are often competitive with random spans, their performance is not consistent; for instance, masking noun phrases achieves parity with random spans on NewsQA, but underperforms on TriviaQA (-1.1% F1).
Adding SBO further improves performance, with a substantial gain on coreference resolution (+2.7% F1) over span masking alone.

MRQA changed the original datasets to unify them into the same format, e.g. all the contexts are truncated to a maximum of 800 tokens and only answerable questions are kept.: NewsQA , SearchQA , TriviaQA , HotpotQA and Natural Questions .
Instead, we always take sequences of up to 512 tokens until it reaches a document boundary. We refer readers to liu2019roberta for further discussion on these modifications and their effects.
As in BERT, the learning rate is warmed up over the first 10,000 steps to a peak value of 1e-4, and then linearly decayed. We retain hyperparameters ( , ) and a decoupled weight decay of .

We deviate from the optimization by running for 2.4M steps and using an epsilon of 1e-8 for AdamW , which converges to a better set of model parameters. Our implementation uses a batch size of 256 sequences with a maximum of 512 tokens. For the SBO, we use 200 dimension position embeddings to mark positions relative to the left boundary token.

assumptions.sentence: We expect that the span selection tasks, question answering and coreference resolution, will particularly benefit from our span-based pre-training.
